user.title: Create a push source
user.description: Choose how HTTP Data Bridge should learn the JSON structure. Live capture is the simplest option when the sender can already make a test request.

data.sample_method: How should the payload be discovered?

data_description.source_name: A friendly name for this external data source.
data_description.sample_method: Capture a real test request, or paste an example JSON payload instead.
data_description.stale_after: Seconds without a valid payload before the selected entities become unavailable. Use 0 to keep the last values available indefinitely.
data_description.local_only: Reject requests that do not come from the local network. Leave this off if an internet-hosted service needs to send data. When Home Assistant Cloud is available, HTTP Data Bridge automatically uses a Nabu Casa cloudhook.
data_description.enabled: Disable this source without deleting its mappings, entities, or webhook ID.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure push source
reconfigure.description: Change source settings and decide whether to keep the current entity mappings or rediscover them from a new payload. The source ID and real webhook ID are preserved.

data_description.sample_method: Keep the existing mappings, or replace them by capturing/pasting a new payload.
data_description.stale_after: Seconds without a valid payload before the selected entities become unavailable. Use 0 to disable expiry.
data_description.local_only: Reject requests that do not come from the local network. When disabled and Home Assistant Cloud is available, the shown webhook URL is a Nabu Casa cloudhook.
data_description.enabled: Disable this source without deleting its mappings, entities, or webhook ID.

sample.title: Paste example JSON
sample.description: Paste one representative payload. It is used only while this setup flow is open and is not saved in the source configuration.

data_description.sample_payload: Objects and arrays are inspected recursively. You can expose individual values, a structured object/array, or the complete payload.

capture.title: Send one test request
capture.description:
Send a JSON POST to the temporary capture URL below, then choose **Continue**.

`{capture_url}`

This temporary endpoint is only for setup and is removed when you continue or leave the flow. The source's permanent webhook URL is shown before saving.

select_fields.title: Choose values
select_fields.description: Select what should become Home Assistant entities. You can choose scalar values, nested objects/arrays, or `$` for the complete JSON payload. Structured or long values can be stored in a sensor attribute.

data_description.platform: Sensor is for ordinary values. Binary sensor is available for JSON true/false and represents an on/off state.

configure_sensor.title: Sensor storage
configure_sensor.description:
{storage_guidance}

Home Assistant sensor states are limited to {state_limit} characters. With attribute storage enabled, the sensor state is the time the value was received and the complete JSON value is available in the `value` attribute.

data_description.store_in_attribute: Use this for long text, objects, arrays, or a complete JSON payload. The `value` attribute is excluded from Recorder history to avoid database growth.
data_description.unit: Optional for a normal numeric sensor. Units are not available when the value is stored in an attribute because the sensor state becomes a timestamp.

error.payload_too_large: The example payload is too large. The maximum size is 256 KiB.
error.no_payload_received: No valid payload has been captured yet. Send a JSON POST to the temporary URL, then continue.
error.binary_requires_boolean: Only JSON true/false values can be configured as binary sensors.
error.attribute_required: This example cannot fit safely in a normal Home Assistant sensor state. Keep attribute storage enabled.
error.attribute_cannot_have_unit: Remove the unit or disable attribute storage. Attribute-backed sensors use a timestamp as their state.
